chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all from al-Fatah ibn Yazid al-Jurjani, who said:

The road brought me together with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) during my return from Mecca to Khurasan, while he was travelling to Iraq. I heard him saying: 'Whoever fears God will be feared, and whoever obeys God will be obeyed.'

So I approached him subtly, arrived, greeted him, and he returned my greeting. Then he said: 'O Fatah! Whoever pleases the Creator will not care about the anger of the creatures, and whoever angers the Creator deserves that God unleash the anger of the creatures upon him.'

And indeed the Creator cannot be described except by what He Himself has described Himself with — and how can One be described Whom the senses are unable to perceive, imaginations unable to grasp, passing thoughts unable to delimit, and visions unable to encompass? He is more Majestic than what the describers describe Him as, and more Exalted than what the characterisers characterise.

He is distant in His closeness and near in His distance — so in His distance He is near, and in His closeness He is far. He established the 'how', so one cannot ask 'how'; and He established the 'where', so one cannot ask 'where' — for He transcends how-ness and where-ness.

key_terms.الأينونية: Where-ness / locality — the philosophical category of place or location, which is inapplicable to God
key_terms.التقوى: Taqwa — God-consciousness, piety; the quality of fearing God that protects one from fearing creation
key_terms.الخالق: The Creator — a Divine name emphasising God's creative sovereignty over all existence
key_terms.الكيفوفية: How-ness / modality — the philosophical category of quality or manner, which cannot be predicated of God
key_terms.سخط المخلوق: The wrath of the creature — the anger of created beings, which holds no ultimate power over one who has earned God's pleasure

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about pleasing God versus fearing creation?
ai.summary: This hadith records a chance encounter between al-Fatah ibn Yazid al-Jurjani and Imam al-Ridha (AS) during a journey from Mecca. The Imam teaches a profound two-part lesson: first, the practical principle that pleasing God immunises one against human opposition, and angering God invites it; second, a sophisticated apophatic theology asserting that God transcends all categories of human thought — sense-perception, imagination, fleeting notions, and vision — and that questions of 'how' and 'where' are inapplicable to the Divine. The encounter illustrates the Imam's role as a living teacher accessible on the road, and the theology reflects classical Shia kalami emphasis on Divine transcendence (tanzih).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Al Mukhtar Bin Muhammad Bin Al Mukhtar and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Abdullah Bin Al Hassan Al Alawy, altogether from Al Fatah Bin Yazeed Al Jurjany who said,

‘I came across Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> in the road during my going from Makkah to Khurasan, and he<sup>asws</sup> was travelling to Al-Iraq, and I head him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who fears Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be feared, and the one who obeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be obeyed’.

So I was subtle regarding the arrival to him<sup>asws</sup>, and I arrived and greeted upon him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>as</sup> responded the greeting upon me, then said: ‘O Fatah! The one who Pleases the Creator would not care about the anger of the creatures, and the one who Angers the Creator, so he would be deserving that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Causes the angers of the people to overcome him.

And the Creator cannot be described except with what He<sup>azwj</sup> Described with Himself<sup>azwj</sup> as, and what is the description of the One<sup>azwj</sup> Whom the sensory perceptions are unable from realizing, and the imaginations of Grasping Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the passing thoughts to limit Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the visions from envisaging Him<sup>azwj</sup>. He<sup>azwj</sup> is more Majestic from what the describers are describing Him<sup>azwj</sup> as, and more Exalted from what the characterisers are characterising.

He is remote in His<sup>azwj</sup> closeness and close by in His<sup>azwj</sup> remoteness, so He<sup>azwj</sup> is close by in His<sup>azwj</sup> remoteness and remote in His<sup>azwj</sup> nearness. He<sup>azwj</sup> Positioned the ‘how’, so it cannot be said, ‘How’, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Positioned the ‘where’, so it cannot be said, ‘Where’, when He<sup>azwj</sup> is cut-off from the how-ness and the where-ness’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Hassan al-‘Alawi all from al-Fath ibn Yazid al-Jurjani who has said the following.

“A road on my way back from Makkah to Khuransan joined me with Imam abu al-Hassan (a.s.) the 2nd who was going to Iraq and I heard him saying, “Whoever observes piety before Allah he is protected and whoever obeys Allah he is obeyed.”

I calmly walked to him and on reaching him I offered my salutation and he responded likewise and said, “O fath whoever pleases Allah is not worried about the anger of people. Whoever causes the Creator to become angry with him he deserves that Allah would cause to subject him to the anger of the people.

One can only speak of the attributes of the Creator the way he Himself has spoken about Himself. How can a person speak of One from Whose perceiving all the senses are frustrated and even the imagination is not able to comprehend Him or ones sharp feelings would reach Him in any way or manner or the eyes would limit Him in any manner. He is far above the description of those who speak of His attributes and the praise of those who speak of His praise.

He is far in His nearness and is near in His being far. He in His far-ness is near and is far in His nearness. He is the condition of the conditions and no one can say that He is in a condition or is somewhere. No one can about Him where because He is far above the conditions and places.”
